Our Amada LC Alpha IV 4Kw CO2 laser uses a concentrated beam of light focused through a cutting lens to cut through metal with exceptional precision. This process is ideal for both simple and complex profiles, eliminating the need for expensive tooling.

What is CNC Milling?

CNC milling is the process of forming a component using a high-speed spindle and specialised cutting tools, controlled by pre-programmed computer software. The CNC system dictates the precise movement of tools and machinery, enabling complex three-dimensional cutting tasks to be completed in a single setup. Excess material is removed as chips or shavings to produce the finished component shape.

This computer-controlled approach delivers significant advantages over manual machining: superior accuracy, excellent repeatability, faster cycle times for complex work, and the ability to produce geometries that would be impossible or impractical to achieve by hand.

Our CNC Milling Capability

At the heart of our milling department are our XYZ 710 and XYZ 510 CNC vertical machining centres, robust and accurate machines capable of handling a wide range of component sizes and materials. Complementing these, our Bridgeport and XYZ manual mills provide versatile manual milling capability for secondary operations and bespoke work.

We mill a comprehensive range of materials including mild steel, stainless steel, aluminium, brass, and engineering plastics. Our tooling inventory and experienced programmers ensure that each material is machined with optimal parameters for the best surface finish and dimensional accuracy, with tolerances achievable to +/- 0.01mm.

CNC Milling Applications

Our CNC milling services cover a wide range of operations including face milling, slot milling, pocket milling, drilling, boring, tapping, thread milling, profile milling, and complex 3D surface machining. Whether your component requires simple flat surfaces and holes or intricate three-dimensional contours, our programming and machining capability can deliver.

CAD/CAM Integration

This integration between design and manufacturing ensures efficient programming, reduced cycle times, and consistent quality. Our programmers work closely with our machinists to establish the most efficient manufacturing approach for each component.

Accuracy and Quality

Our CNC milling processes are designed to achieve zero defects. Pre-programmed software ensures precise, repeatable specifications every time. Combined with our quality inspection procedures, this delivers components that consistently meet your dimensional and surface finish requirements.

Cost-Effective Production

CNC milling is inherently cost-effective due to minimal material waste, fast cycle times, and reduced manual intervention. Whether you need a single prototype or a production batch, our CNC milling service delivers value.

Romark Engineering provides specialist aluminium welding services to businesses across London from our workshop in Stanford-Le-Hope, Essex. Aluminium welding demands specific skills, equipment, and techniques that differ significantly from steel welding, and our experienced welders have the expertise to deliver clean, strong aluminium welds for a wide range of applications.

Why Aluminium Welding Requires Specialist Skills

Aluminium presents unique challenges for welding. Its high thermal conductivity means heat dissipates quickly, requiring more heat input than similarly sized steel components. The oxide layer on aluminium's surface melts at a much higher temperature than the base metal, requiring proper cleaning and the right welding technique to achieve a sound joint. Aluminium's lower melting point also means it is more susceptible to burn-through and distortion if welding parameters are not carefully controlled.

Our welders understand these challenges and have the training and experience to produce consistent, high-quality aluminium welds. Whether you need thin gauge sheet metal joints or heavier structural connections, we select the appropriate technique and parameters for your specific application.

TIG Welding for Aluminium

TIG (Tungsten Inert Gas) welding is our primary process for aluminium fabrication. Using AC TIG welding, the alternating current provides the cleaning action needed to break down the aluminium oxide layer while maintaining stable arc control. This produces clean, precise welds with excellent penetration and minimal distortion.

TIG welding is particularly suited to aluminium sheet metal work where appearance and precision are important. The process gives the welder full control over heat input and filler addition, enabling neat, consistent welds on thin gauge materials where burn-through is a risk with other processes.

MIG Welding for Aluminium

For heavier aluminium sections and higher production volumes, we also offer MIG (Metal Inert Gas) welding. MIG welding provides faster deposition rates than TIG, making it efficient for larger fabrications and structural aluminium work. Our MIG equipment is set up for aluminium wire feeding, with the specialist liners and drive rolls required for reliable aluminium wire delivery.

Applications

Our aluminium welding services support a wide range of London applications including architectural metalwork, balustrades, handrails, signage, display structures, vehicle bodies and components, marine fittings, food processing equipment, electrical enclosures, and bespoke fabrications. We work with common aluminium grades including 1050, 5083, 5251, 6061, and 6082.

Complete Aluminium Fabrication Service

Our Amada laser cuts aluminium sheet, our CNC press brakes fold it to precise angles, and our machining department handles any milling or turning operations required. Romark Engineering provides expert sheet metal work from our fully equipped workshop in Stanford-Le-Hope, Essex. Serving the automotive, power generation, and architectural industries, we deliver high-quality sheet metal components and assemblies from single prototypes through to ongoing production supply.

What is Sheet Metal Work?

Sheet metal work encompasses the processes of cutting, forming, and joining flat sheets of metal into three-dimensional components and assemblies. At Romark Engineering, we carry out all the core sheet metal processes in-house: laser cutting for accurate flat profiles, CNC press brake folding for precision bends and forms, and welding for joining components into finished assemblies. This complete in-house capability allows us to control quality throughout the manufacturing process and deliver finished components ready for use.

Laser Cutting

Our Amada LC Alpha IV 4Kw CO2 laser is the starting point for most sheet metal work. It produces clean, accurate profiles in mild steel up to 12mm, stainless steel up to 12mm, and aluminium, copper, and brass at various thicknesses. Cutting tolerances of +/- 0.1mm ensure that blanks are accurate before moving to the forming stage. We accept DXF and DWG file formats, or our CAD team creates cutting programs from your drawings.

CNC Folding

Our Amada CNC press brakes, with capacities from 100 to 220 tons and folding lengths up to 4 metres, handle the forming stage of sheet metal work. CNC back gauge systems deliver repeatable accuracy on every bend, whether we are folding a prototype or the hundredth part in a production run. Our operators produce simple single bends, complex multi-bend components, box sections, enclosures, and formed profiles.

Welding

Our coded welders complete the sheet metal work process by joining folded components into finished assemblies. TIG welding provides clean, precise joints for stainless steel and aluminium work. MIG welding handles heavier materials and structural applications efficiently. Spot welding delivers fast, reliable joints for production sheet metal assemblies.

Blank Development

Accurate sheet metal work begins with accurate blanks. Our CAD department develops flat patterns from 3D models, calculating bend allowances and deductions so that components fold to the correct finished dimensions first time. This eliminates trial-and-error and reduces material waste, saving time and cost particularly on complex multi-bend components.

Materials

We carry out sheet metal work in mild steel, stainless steel, and aluminium as standard. Our laser also cuts copper and brass. We work with material thicknesses from thin gauge sheet through to heavy plate, selecting the appropriate processes for each material and thickness combination.

Applications

Our sheet metal work produces components for a diverse range of applications including enclosures, housings, brackets, panels, machine guards, ventilation ductwork, architectural features, signage, electrical cabinets, covers, trays, and bespoke components. We work from your drawings or can develop designs in-house using Solidworks, AutoCAD, and Rhino3D.
